title: Claims-check record header (studies#160)
description: YAML header of studies/<study>/analysis/provenance/claims_check_<rN>_<date>[_<k>].md, written by studies/util/claims_check.py write_record(). It keys one claims-check run to the report content and the evidence the reviewer read.

report.description: study-relative path of the report checked

content_digest.description: sha256 of the report's claims + body (claims_check.content_digest)

inputs.description: repository-relative path -> evidence digest of the starting points and every file a verdict cites (never the report itself): an analysis JSON's body without _meta (_meta.body_digest), else the file's sha256; checked for staleness

context.description: repository-relative path -> sha256 of reading context (CONTEXT.md, a study README/PLAN/CHANGELOG); recorded, never checked for staleness

code.description: repository-relative path -> sha256 of code the reviewer read (.py files, e.g. producers); recorded, never checked for staleness: a code change that alters a number or a sentence shows in the JSON body or the report text (studies#164)

rubric_version.description: claims-check/2 adds the reviewer writing its output to a named file and a blocking tag per finding (studies#164); claims-check/3 replaces blocking with item (C0-C9) and severity High/Medium/Low (studies#167)

prompt_sha256.description: sha256 of the prompt as given

response_sha256.description: sha256 of the response as returned

severity_counts.description: claims-check/3 on: the response's findings by severity (an entry is a finding when its severity is not null); absent for older rubrics; recorded, never checked (studies#167)
